fields.reasoning: Intent: the sibling change sets carved out of accepted umbrellas this session (code anchors 01M6HJX, unclaimed changes 01M6HKR) both serve model-tells-truth, and text-references' own statement (a rename never breaks a sentence) is about the model staying true; anyone-builds is the umbrella's broader root and adds nothing here. The carving guide says carve keeps IDs and links and that an emptied source is withdrawn by hand, and references-by-id is landed so the decided-by link applies in the target. Stored form: references-by-id says stored by ID, shown by handle; a bracketed @{ID} cannot collide with the '@' already in the log (emails, checkout@v7, '@key'), and requiring whitespace or ( [ before @ keeps those three from being read as references even on new writes. Verbatim fields are skipped because the hard rule is never to alter an owner's exact words, and sources are scrubbed transcripts. Refusing an unresolvable reference mirrors how a link to a node the write may not see is refused, and keeps a dangling reference from ever being written; @@ gives an escape so a literal @word can still be written. Resolving an input @{ID} like any reference, rather than passing it through as already-stored text, keeps a hand-typed @{BOGUS} from being stored unrefused; re-escaping a literal @ as @@ on display keeps a stored literal @word from being read back as a reference. Showing by current handle in both text and JSON makes output round-trip through a later write. A missing node in check is a fail because the capability exists so sentences never break, while a retired target is still a real node, so only a warn. Only a full 26-character ID inside @{ } counts as stored form because landed text, this plan's own included, already holds look-alikes such as '@{ID}' and '@{BOGUS}', and check must stay clean on it; such legacy text is shown with its @ re-escaped, which keeps the round trip. A retired target is shown by full ID, not handle, because Resolve matches handles only among live nodes, so a shown @<handle> would be refused or would silently bind to a live node that has since taken the handle; keeping an already-stored retired reference on write lets that shown text go back to its field. Every read operation that prints node text shows handles, not only the original five, because references-by-id says references are shown by handle without exception, and search over shown text keeps '@handle' searchable.
fields.statement: (1) Intent and leaf: the change set serves the landed root intent model-tells-truth, and the leaf comes over with rhiza carve text-references --from 01M5SWSWDVB237 --to 01M6HNNWFR1J2AHQRNKFTPME46, which keeps its ID and moves its decided-by link to references-by-id; the umbrella, left with no ops, is withdrawn. (2) Stored form and scanned fields: a write (node add or set) scans every string-valued field of a node, except the verbatim fields quote, quote_where and wording and every field of a source node, which are stored exactly as given. A reference starts with @ at the start of the text or after whitespace or an opening ( or [, followed by a handle (lower-case words joined by dashes), a node ID or unique ID prefix of 4+ characters, or the stored form {<full node ID>}; so emails, checkout@v7 and a quoted '@key' are not references. @@ writes a literal @ and is never resolved. Each reference is stored as @{<full node ID>}, and only @{ followed by a full 26-character node ID and } counts as a stored reference; any other @{...} in stored text (such as '@{ID}' or '@{BOGUS}' in prose) is literal text; an @{<ID>} in a write's input is a reference like any other, resolved and refused by the same rule, so hand-typed stored form cannot bypass resolution; json_fields and links are not scanned. Already-landed entries are never rewritten; they hold no stored reference (no @{<26-character ID>} is in the log today), and their literal @ that would start a reference is shown re-escaped (old '@word' as '@@word', '@{ID}' as '@@{ID}'), which written back stores the same literal text. (3) Unresolvable reference: the write is refused whole (not found, exit 4), naming each reference that names no node the write may refer to; the rule is the same as for a link's ends: landed nodes and nodes of the write's own change set, live and not retired, except that a reference to a retired node is kept when the field's current stored value already holds that same ID, so text that already refers to a node retired since is not refused when written back to its field. The error's next says to fix the handle or write @@ for a literal @. (4) Display and check: every read operation that prints a node's text fields (render, show, why, slice, ls, tree, search, inbox, feed, roadmap, change show and change diff, the last two in the change set's view) and the read apps, text and --json alike, show each @{ID} naming a live node as @<the node's current handle> in that view and re-escape as @@ each stored literal @ that would otherwise start a reference, so the shown text written back to the same field in that view stores the same text; a reference to a retired node is shown as @{<full ID>} (handles resolve only among live nodes, so @<handle> could not round-trip) and written back to its field is kept by rule (3); a reference that does not resolve in the view is shown as @{<full ID>}, and writing that back is refused like any unresolvable reference. search matches its query against the shown text, so a search for '@other' finds a stored reference to other. rhiza check scans the folded model's stored references (@{<26-character ID>} only), each in the view of the change set that wrote it: an ID that names no node is a fail finding (a dangling reference), naming the node, field and ID; an ID that names a retired node is a warn.

fields.acceptance: Unit tests in internal/textref: a reference starts with @ at the start of the text or after whitespace or an opening ( or [ and is followed by a handle (lower-case words joined by single dashes) or an ID or 4+ character ID prefix; darin@hey.com, checkout@v7 and '@key' contain no reference; @@ yields a literal @ and is never a reference; a resolver given a lookup rewrites every reference, @{<ID>} included, to @{<full ID>} and returns each unresolved one with its offset, so @{BOGUS} is unresolved; a formatter treats only @{<26-character ID>} in stored text as a reference, shows it as @<handle> when the lookup gives a live node's handle and as @{<full ID>} when the node is retired or the lookup has none, and treats stored '@{ID}', '@{BOGUS}' and '@{<full ID>}' as literal text shown as '@@{ID}' etc.; and shows a stored literal @ that would start a reference (from @@word) as @@; a fuzz test checks that formatting resolved text, literal @ included, and resolving it again yields the same stored text
fields.statement: One pure package, internal/textref, finds the references in a text and turns them both ways: @handle, @<ID or 4+ character ID prefix> and @{<ID>} to stored @{<full ID>}, and stored @{<full 26-character ID>} back to @<current handle> of a live node (or @{<full ID>} for a retired or missing one); any other @{...} in stored text is literal, with @@ for a literal @ both ways (the formatter re-escapes a literal @ that would start a reference)

fields.acceptance: text-refs-write.txtar: rhiza add capability with statement 'Builds on @other' stores @{<other's full ID>} in the log entry; an ID prefix reference stores the full ID; a reference to a node of the write's own change set resolves, one to a node of another unlanded change set or a newly referenced retired node does not; after other is retired, rhiza set of a field that already stores @{<other's ID>} with input @{<other's full ID>} keeps it, and adding that reference to a different field or node is refused; quote, quote_where, wording and a source's fields are stored verbatim; '@@' stores a literal @; an input @{<other's full ID>} stores the same ID, and an input @{BOGUS} is refused like any unresolvable reference; an unresolvable reference exits 4 with code not_found naming each bad reference and its field, with a next saying to fix the handle or write @@, and writes nothing; --dry-run reports the same refusal; the same file through rhiza apply behaves the same; describe-golden.txtar is regenerated if a request or response type changes; the rhiza guide's skill text tells agents to write @handle to refer to a node
fields.statement: rhiza add and set, and add and set items of rhiza apply, resolve the references in every string-valued field of a node (except quote, quote_where, wording and every field of a source node) at write time and store each as @{<full ID>}, refusing the whole write when one names no node it may refer to; a reference to a retired node is refused unless the field's current stored value already holds that same ID, in which case it is kept

fields.acceptance: text-refs-display.txtar: after a node's statement refers to @other and other is renamed to renamed, rhiza show, why, slice, ls, tree, search, inbox, feed, roadmap, change show and change diff print @renamed wherever they print that statement, in markdown and in --json fields; rhiza search '@renamed' finds the node; rhiza render writes @renamed into the rendered page; a read app's --once JSON (rhiza tui app <read app> --once) shows @renamed; a reference to a node not in the view shows @{<full ID>}; after other is retired the reference shows @{<other's full ID>} and writing the shown statement back with rhiza set stores the same text; a log entry written by hand before the feature with '@word' and '@{ID}' in a statement shows '@@word' and '@@{ID}', and writing that back stores the same literal text; a statement written with '@@word' stores a literal @word and is shown as @@word; copying the shown text into rhiza set stores the same text (same IDs, literal @ kept literal)
fields.statement: Every read operation that prints a node's text fields (render, show, why, slice, ls, tree, search, inbox, feed, roadmap, change show and change diff, the last two in the change set's view) and the read apps, in text and --json alike, show each stored @{<26-character ID>} as @<the node's current handle> in that view when it names a live node, and as @{<full ID>} when it names a retired node or does not resolve there; search matches its query against this shown text; and show a stored literal @ that would start a reference as @@

fields.acceptance: Unit tests in internal/check: a stored @{ID} naming no node gives one fail finding under a new rule text-ref, naming the node, the field and the ID, and sets Report.OK false; one naming a retired node gives a warn and keeps OK true; resolving references, text with no @{, and literal look-alikes such as '@{ID}', '@{BOGUS}' and '@{<full ID>}' give nothing; check-text-refs.txtar: a log entry written by hand with a dangling @{ID} makes rhiza check exit non-zero with that finding; the new rule appears in check.Rules() and in describe output; rhiza check on this repo stays clean, this plan's own statements and acceptances (which hold such look-alikes) included
fields.statement: rhiza check scans the folded model's stored references (only @{<full 26-character ID>}; other @{...} text is literal), each in the view of the change set that wrote it, and fails on one naming no node and warns on one naming a retired node
